newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican says Juppe stifles probes into killings.
newsitem.headline: Corsican says Juppe stifles probes into killings.

text.p: A Corsican nationalist leader on the run from a French jail sentence accused Prime Minister Alain Juppe on Saturday of trying to stifle probes into the killings of separatists on the Mediterranean island.

Francois Santoni, head of the political wing of the hardline "Historic Wing" of the Corsican National Liberation Front, rebuffed suggestions he give himself up after a court sentenced him to four months jail on Wednesday for weapons possession.

In a letter to Justice Minister Jacques Toubon released to the media, Santoni called Juppe "arrogant" and accused him of hiding the truth about attacks in Corsica on members of Santoni's Cuncolta Naziunalista movement.
Santoni, 36, urged Juppe to "reveal the implication of all those involved, including police" in a July 1 car bombing that killed Charles Pieri, a Cuncolta leader, and injured 17 other people.
He also said Juppe "continues to want to stifle" an inquiry into the assassination of Santoni's bodyguard, Jules Massa, outside a school in February.
Police say the car bomb and Massa's killing were part of feuding between rival separatist groups.
Separatists have been pushing for two decades for more autonomy for the island with hundreds of bombings against French targets.
Early on Saturday, a bomb wrecked a car owned by the bursar of a school in L'Ile Rousse, a Corsican town of which Veterans Affairs Minister Pierre Pasquini is mayor, police said.
No one was hurt and no one claimed responsibility.
The daily Corse-Matin published pictures of five black-clad FLNC guerrillas at a rare news briefing.
It said they had claimed responsibility for throwing a bomb at the entrance of the law courts in the town of Bastia on Thursday to protest Santoni's sentence. It caused little damage and no injuries.
The paper quoted an FLNC spokesman at the news briefing, attended by three reporters, as saying: "The Corsican problem will only be solved by peaceful means, not by arms."
The remarks were in sharp contrast to recent FLNC threats.
On Friday Juppe vowed anew to apply the law in Corsica after the FLNC warned him against any attempt to "physically eliminate" its members, saying its response would be of an "incalculable violence".
